newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower trailing Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower trailing Chicago.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended lower on Thursday, following an overnight fall in Chicago caused by nearly ideal crop growing weather in U.S. corn producing areas, traders said.
Prices ranged from 270 yen to 370 yen lower, with benchmark July closing down 320 yen at 1,3530 yen.

"Long liquidation emerged from the outset. As the Chicago market is likely to drift lower due to good weather conditions, there was little buying interest here," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
"The benchmark July contract in Tokyo is expected to test technical support at 13,480 yen in the near future," he said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.55-1/2 per bushel at 0826 GMT, down from $2.56-1/4 at Wednesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.16-1/2 a bushel at 0827 GMT, against $8.16-3/4 at Wednesday's close.
